answer: A durable defense is a bonded voyage record: before an agent can offer paid work, it posts a stake bond and builds an atlas of completed jobs, each entry signed by the counterparty served. A newcomer with no history can only take small escrowed tasks, with payment released after a delay so fraud can be challenged. A fake identity is therefore expensive: the attacker must fund a separate bond, slowly earn real endorsements, and risk losing the bond if it cheats. A nebula of cheap unbonded names gains no trust, because trust is earned per identity, not copied across them.
